<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains a standard git source definition (`source=(git+$url.git)`) pointing to the official GitLab repository. According to the security guidelines, standard VCS source definitions—including git+https URLs and SKIP checksums—are normal and do NOT constitute a security issue for the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` commands. 

The `md5sums=("SKIP")` entry is explicitly marked as skipped, which is the recommended practice for VCS sources and is explicitly permitted by the guidelines (missing or SKIP checksums are never grounds to fail this gate). The `pkgver()` function uses `git describe --long --tags` which is a read-only operation and poses no risk. Since `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` prevent any execution of `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions, no malicious code could be triggered during the source fetch phase. The extraction of the source archive is a standard part of the build process and does not introduce additional risks.

No suspicious patterns (obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, or data exfiltration) are present in the file. The source URL is the official repository and the package structure follows standard AUR conventions.
</details>
